newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed down across the board on Friday mainly due to a slump on the domestic A share markets, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded seven-day contract fell to 8.01 percent from 8.20 percent on Thursday.
Total turnover of the six-contract market rose to 5.6 million lots from 3.9 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
China's stock markets plunged on Friday after Beijing announced a huge quota for new share issues.
"The plunge greatly dampened sentiment on the repo market," said one trader. "Institutions are worried about the near-term trend for both the stock markets and the repo market."

One new A share issue in Shanghai on Friday supported early-maturing contracts, in particular the seven-day contract, for most of the session, but it failed to push the contracts up at the close due to weak sentiment, traders said.
Traders said movements of the repo rates in the short term will heavily depend on the performance of the stock markets.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed on Friday after the rises of the past few days, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 fell slightly to 120.82 yuan from 120.90 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market fell to 1.1 million lots from 1.3 million lots.
Traders said that with the A share markets falling, some investors were returning their funds to the spot market, which had enlivened the market.
They said they believed the spot contracts would rise slightly next week.
